meta.title: Heritage Revitalization
meta.topic: Transforming historic industrial buildings into vibrant creative hubs while preserving local identity.

script.text: Hong Kong Diploma of Secondary Education Examination 2026. English Language Paper 3. Listening and Integrated Skills. Heritage Revitalization - High Stamina Mock Exam. This recording will be played once only.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: The entire broadcast will last approximately one hour and fifteen minutes. Part A. Task 1. You are a student volunteer helping at the Heritage Council. You will hear an interview between the volunteer coordinator, Emily Cheung, and an applicant, Adrian Ho. Complete the registration form. You now have two minutes to study the task. (120-second pause)

script.speaker: Emily
script.text: Good afternoon! You must be Adrian. Come in, have a seat. I'm Emily Cheung, the lead coordinator for our Heritage Revitalization volunteer core. We're very excited to have some new blood in the team, especially with the Old Harbour project launching soon.

script.speaker: Adrian
script.text: Thank you, Emily. It's great to be here. I've been following the project in the architectural journals for months. My name is Adrian Ho—that's H-O, just two letters! Short and simple.

script.speaker: Emily
script.text: H-O. Got it. And I have your contact number from your initial web form as 6221 8890. Is that still the best way to reach you? We do a lot of our coordination via SMS and WhatsApp.

script.speaker: Adrian
script.text: Yes, that's my main mobile. And yes, I'm very active on WhatsApp. For my current status, I'm a final-year architecture student over at HKU. I'm specializing in urban conservation, so this project is basically my dream internship, even if it's 'just' volunteering.

script.speaker: Emily
script.text: An architecture student! That's perfect. We always need people who can actually read the blueprints. Now, since we deal with a lot of international tourists and local residents, what's your language proficiency like? Are you comfortable giving tours in multiple languages?

script.speaker: Adrian
script.text: I'm fluent in both English and Cantonese. My Mandarin is okay for basic directions, but for the complex historical stuff, I'd prefer to stick to English and Cantonese if possible.

script.speaker: Emily
script.text: That's exactly what we need. Most of our Heritage Walks are conducted in those two languages. Have you done any volunteering like this before? Any sites we might know?

script.speaker: Adrian
script.text: I spent six months at Tai Kwun last year. I was part of the heritage education team there. It taught me a lot about the 'Adaptive Reuse' model and how to handle large crowds in narrow historical corridors.

script.speaker: Emily
script.text: Tai Kwun is a gold standard. If you can handle the crowds there on a Saturday afternoon, you can handle anything! Which specific area of the Old Harbour project interests you most? We have the maritime history section, the residential blocks, and the industrial quarter.

script.speaker: Adrian
script.text: The Industrial Heritage quarter, definitely. I'm fascinated by the old Textile Mills and the way they've been converted. I'd love to focus on that. Honestly, my main motivation for joining is career networking. I hope to work for a firm like Marcus Thorne's one day, and I've heard he's often at the site meetings.

script.speaker: Emily
script.text: Marcus is there almost every Tuesday! You'll definitely see him. Now, for availability, our peak times are the weekends. When are you most free?

script.speaker: Adrian
script.text: I have studio classes on Saturdays, but I'm completely free on Sunday afternoons. I can commit to a four-hour block every week. And since I live in Pok Fu Lam, I usually take the MTR to the site—it's very convenient.

script.speaker: Emily
script.text: Sunday afternoon, MTR. Noted. Do you have any special skills you'd like to offer? Aside from the tour guiding?

script.speaker: Adrian
script.text: I'm a keen amateur photographer. I have a professional-grade DSLR and I'd be happy to take high-quality photos for the project's social media pages or the volunteer newsletter.

script.speaker: Emily
script.text: That would be incredible! Our current newsletter photos are... well, they're a bit blurry. One more thing, Adrian. We need to be aware of any health conditions for our site-safety protocols. Any allergies or issues with being outdoors for long periods?

script.speaker: Adrian
script.text: I have a bit of a pollen allergy in the spring, but as long as we're not doing the garden tours for three hours straight, I'm usually fine with my inhaler.

script.speaker: Emily
script.text: Pollen allergy. Noted. We'll keep you away from the botanical section in April! For your uniform, I'll need your size. We provide the green polo shirts.

script.speaker: Adrian
script.text: Medium, please. And I assume there's no registration fee since I'm a student?

script.speaker: Emily
script.text: Exactly. The $100 processing fee is completely exempt for students and seniors. Well, Adrian, you're all set. We'll see you at the orientation next month!

script.speaker: Adrian
script.text: Thanks, Emily! Really looking forward to it.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Task 2. Listen to a presentation by Marcus Thorne, Architectural Director, on 'Adaptive Reuse: The Invisible Engineering of 2026'. Complete the notes. You now have two minutes to study the task. (120-second pause)

script.speaker: Marcus Thorne
script.text: Good morning. When people think of heritage, they think of dusty museums. But in 2026, heritage is alive. It's functional. It's 'Adaptive Reuse'. I want to walk you through the journey of the Old Harbour project. Our journey began with a massive team effort, and I have to credit our lead historical consultant, Alistair Montgomery. He's the one who dug through the 19th-century archives to find the original blueprints for the Customs House.

script.speaker: Marcus Thorne
script.text: The project itself dates back to the 2015 Proposal. That was when the city first realized that these industrial shells weren't just decay—they were opportunity. But it wasn't an easy sell. To get the local community on board, we had to make a significant concession: thirty percent of the total floor space was dedicated to non-profit community arts and a public museum. This was the 'Social Contract' that allowed the 2015 Proposal to proceed.

script.speaker: Marcus Thorne
script.text: We finally broke ground in the Spring of 2017. If you remember that year, it was a particularly wet spring, which made the stabilization work incredibly difficult. The foundation of the main pier was literally sinking into the silt. To save it, we had to adhere to a very specific, and quite frankly, very annoying regulation: Building Code REV-772-B. This code is the 'Bible' for seismic retrofitting in historical zones. It forbids any visible steel supports on the exterior.

script.speaker: Marcus Thorne
script.text: So, how do you reinforce a 150-year-old wall without showing the steel? We used a method called 'core-drilling'. We drilled vertically through the center of the masonry—sometimes thirty feet deep—and inserted high-tensile rods. We then secured them with a specialized epoxy resin. This is what I call 'Invisible Engineering'. It allows the building to withstand a magnitude 7 earthquake while looking exactly as it did in 1892. The grand reveal, or what we called the '2019 Opening', was a watershed moment. We managed to keep the original iron gantries in the atrium, which now serve as the framework for our digital art installations.

script.speaker: Marcus Thorne
script.text: Now, we are in the 2024 Expansion phase. We're adding a modern annex to the north side. We've chosen Corten steel for the facade because its natural rust-colored patina perfectly matches the weathered brick of the original buildings. But we aren't just looking back; we're looking up. The expansion is targeting LEED Platinum certification. We've integrated photovoltaic glass that will provide forty percent of the annex's total electrical needs. And most impressively, we've installed a geothermal HVAC system that uses the stable temperature of the earth to heat and cool the entire district. It is a true dialogue with the past, powered by the technology of the future.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Task 3. Listen to a radio debate between Sarah Jenkins, Marcus Thorne, and Elena Rostova. Complete the comparison table. You now have two minutes to study the task. (120-second pause)

script.speaker: Sarah Jenkins
script.text: Welcome to 'City voices'. Today we're debating the $350 Million budget for the Old Harbour District revitalization. Marcus, you've been a proponent of a much leaner, $200 Million 'market-led' approach. Why?

script.speaker: Marcus Thorne
script.text: Sarah, $200 Million is responsible. It focuses on the essentials—safety, infrastructure, and basic repair. If we spend $400 Million, as you initially proposed, we are essentially building a luxury bubble that the city's debt can't sustain. We need to let private developers take some of the weight.

script.speaker: Elena Rostova
script.text: But Marcus, 'letting private developers take the weight' is just code for gentrification! I represent the residents of the Harbour. Their biggest fear is that they'll be priced out of their own homes. If you don't invest in social protections, the 'revitalization' is just a eviction notice in a pretty envelope.

script.speaker: Sarah Jenkins
script.text: This is why we've landed on the compromise budget of $350 Million. It's the 'Integrated Revitalization' model. Let's break it down. $280 Million is earmarked strictly for core structural and heritage restoration—including keeping the Customs House in public hands. Marcus, I know you wanted to sell it to a hotel group, but this committee has decided it must remain a public library and museum.

script.speaker: Marcus Thorne
script.text: $280 Million for bricks and mortar. It's a lot, but I'll concede it's necessary for the Customs House. That leaves $70 Million.

script.speaker: Elena Rostova
script.text: That $70 Million is the 'Community Stabilization Fund'. It's what pays for the rent control measures for the 400 apartments in the district. It ensures that the families who have been there for generations aren't hit by a 30% rent hike the day the ribbon is cut. To pay for this, we're looking at a 30-year bond duration instead of the standard 20. It spreads the cost, but it secures the soul of the district. We are calling it 'Integrated Revitalization' because you cannot separate the buildings from the people.

script.speaker: Sarah Jenkins
script.text: Integrated Revitalization. It's a silver standard that actually protects. Marcus, are you on board?

script.speaker: Marcus Thorne
script.text: If the metrics for success include resident retention, and not just property value, then yes. $350 Million it is.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Task 4. Listen to the emergency briefing for tour guides at the Old Harbour site. Complete the matrix. You now have two minutes to study the task. (120-second pause)

script.speaker: Emily
script.text: Alright team, listen up. With the $350 Million budget finalized, we are moving into the high-security phase of construction. You need to be aware of the 'Heritage Harmony' protocol. This is our internal framework for protecting sensitive historical materials. If you see contractors using heavy power tools near the 1840s masonry, check if they've done their mandatory thermal imaging. We use it to detect moisture pockets that could cause the walls to shatter under vibration.

script.speaker: Emily
script.text: For the aesthetics, all lighting must use the 2700K gas lamp mimicry bulbs. We don't want any harsh blue LEDs ruining the 19th-century vibe. And for any structural repairs, we only use bio-resin acoustic dampeners to isolate the mechanical hum. Now, for the visitors, we have a new incentive: the 'Local Artisan Vouchers'. Every tourist pass comes with a $500 credit that can ONLY be used at our certified legacy merchants. To qualify, a business must prove a ten-year history in the district. It's how we keep the traditional glassblowers and bakers in business.

script.speaker: Emily
script.text: Lastly, emergency safety. If you encounter a medical or structural emergency, use the keyword 'Blue Shield' over the radio. It alerts the heritage police without causing a panic among the tourists. Our primary evacuation route for the industrial quarter is through 'Customs Alley'—do NOT use the main gate as it will be blocked by emergency vehicles. If you have any issues, your primary contact is Elena Rostova. Our next full-scale emergency drill is scheduled for November 12th. We're expecting a massive weekend attendee count of at least 5,000 people once the new pier opens, so we need to be sharp. This briefing is classified, so keep your notes secure. Let's get to work.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: This is the end of Part A. Now, turn to Part B.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Part B. Introduction. You are Chris Wong, an assistant to Elena Rostova. You will hear a briefing Elena gives to the community liaison team. As you listen, take notes which may help you to complete the tasks. You will have five minutes to study the Part B Information Directory and the tasks. (Pause 5m)

script.speaker: Elena Rostova
script.text: Good morning, everyone. As we move into the final phase of the Old Harbour Revitalization, my office is being flooded with questions. Chris, I need you to be my primary filter for these. First, the budget. There's an old 2022 proposal floating around the internet for a 'Sha Tin Cultural Hub' with a budget of $150 Million. PLEASE DISREGARD THIS. That was a completely different project on the Shing Mun Riverfront that never left the planning stage. Our budget for the Old Harbour is $350 Million. If you see any reports mentioning $150 Million or the $200 Million 'market-led' plan, correct them immediately. Our model is the 'Integrated' model.

script.speaker: Elena Rostova
script.text: I want to emphasize the 'Heritage Harmony' protocol. It's not just for the architects; it's for the community's peace of mind. It mandates the use of bio-resin dampeners for all HVAC units. If residents complain about noise, you can tell them that we are using the highest acoustic isolation standards in the city. Also, the 'Local Artisan Vouchers' are our secret weapon against gentrification. Each tourist gets a $500 digital credit. Chris, make sure the merchants know they must have at least ten years of history in the district to be eligible for the city's reimbursement. We already have the fourth-generation glassblower signed up, but we need to reach out to the traditional bakery on Elm Street.

script.speaker: Elena Rostova
script.text: Finally, the Customs House. It will NOT be a hotel. It will be a public heritage center. This is a non-negotiable part of our $280 Million structural allocation. If anyone asks about the 'Blue Shield' keyword, tell them it's our internal safety signal for rapid response. Our goal is to maintain a weekend capacity of 5,000 visitors without losing the neighborhood feel. Chris, I'll need you to draft a formal letter to the contractors by Friday, reminding them that any deviation from the Heritage Harmony lighting or masonry standards will result in an immediate work stoppage. We are preserving a soul here, not just building a facade. Alright, let's look at the community feedback cards...

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: This is the end of the Integrated Skills recording. You now have 1 hour and 15 minutes to complete your tasks. (End of simulation)
